rich_summary: The Creature recounts the moment his hope for human companionship collapses and transforms into vengeance. After the De Lacey family flees in terror, he wanders the forest in a frenzy of rage and despair, ultimately burning their cottage and severing his last emotional tie to humanity. Resolving to confront Victor, he begins a lonely, brutal journey toward Geneva, traveling by night through cold landscapes. A brief return of kindness—saving a drowning girl—ends when he is shot by her guardian, convincing him that humanity will always answer benevolence with violence. Near Geneva he encounters a child, William Frankenstein; realizing the boy belongs to his creator’s family, he kills him and frames Justine by planting a portrait on her. The Creature ends by demanding Victor create a companion like himself.

highlight_spans.why: The Creature’s furious opening curse against Victor captures the emotional core of the chapter: rage at a creator who gave life without compassion.
The early forest wandering—howling under cold stars and raging through the woods—establishes the lonely, almost cosmic isolation that defines the Creature’s transformation.
The section culminating in his vow of 'everlasting war against the species' marks the pivotal psychological turn from wounded outsider to deliberate enemy of humanity.
The burning of the De Lacey cottage is a symbolic act: the destruction of the Creature’s last connection to kindness and the birth of his revenge-driven identity.
The encounter with the drowning girl and the gunshot that follows is a cruel moral test; even his genuine act of rescue is punished, cementing his hatred of humanity.
William’s murder and the framing of Justine represent the Creature’s first deliberate act of revenge against Victor, escalating the tragedy and binding their fates.

top_scenes.scene_text: The Creature dancing in manic fury around the De Lacey cottage as wind howls and flames climb the wooden walls into the night sky.
In a bright spring forest beside a rushing river, the Creature drags a rescued girl from the water just as a man bursts from the trees and fires a gun into his shoulder.
At dusk near Geneva, the towering Creature grips young William in a shadowed field as the boy struggles and the mountains loom in the distance.
